questions.prompt: ____ bist du? — Ich bin Ahmed.
questions.explanation: Wer asks who someone is.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wer bist du? — ____ bin Ahmed.
questions.explanation: Ich is I; it goes with bin.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ ist dein Name? — Mein Name ist Monika.
questions.explanation: Wie ist dein Name? is the name question in the key.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wie ist dein Name? — ____ Name ist Monika.
questions.explanation: Mein Name means my name.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ heißt du? — Ich heiße Omar.
questions.explanation: Use Wie with heißt to ask someone’s name.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ geht es dir? — Danke, gut.
questions.explanation: Wie geht es dir? asks how someone is.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ alt bist du? — Ich bin 7 Jahre alt.
questions.explanation: Wie alt means how old.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wie alt bist du? — Ich ____ 7 Jahre alt.
questions.explanation: Use ich bin, not ich bist or ich ist.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wie alt bist ____? — Ich bin 9.
questions.explanation: Bist is the form used with du.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wie heißt ____? — Ich heiße Hans.
questions.explanation: Heißt is the form used with du in this question.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ du Ali? — Ja, ich bin Ali.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question with du starts with Bist.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Bist du Ali? — ____, ich bin Ali.
questions.explanation: The reply confirms the same name, so it begins Ja.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: ____ du Hans? — Nein, ich heiße Frank.
questions.explanation: Heißt goes with du.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Heißt du Hans? — ____, ich heiße Frank.
questions.explanation: The speaker gives a different name, so the answer begins Nein.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ist dein Name Mona? — Nein, mein Name ist ____ Mona.
questions.explanation: Nein answers the question; nicht negates the name inside the sentence.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ich heiße ____ Maria.
questions.explanation: The supplied key selects Frau in this example.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ich heiße ____ Hans.
questions.explanation: The supplied key selects Herr in this example.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Mein Name ist ____ Adel.
questions.explanation: The supplied key selects Herr. The printed distractor Faru is normalized to Frau.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ich bin ____ Menna.
questions.explanation: The supplied key selects Frau in this example.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Mein Name ____ Paula.
questions.explanation: Mein Name is third-person singular and takes ist.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ich ____ Mona.
questions.explanation: With ich, the form of heißen is heiße.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Ich ____ Anna.
questions.explanation: With ich, use bin.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Mein Vater heißt ____ Ahmed.
questions.explanation: Vater means father; the key uses the title Herr.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Meine Tante heißt ____ Maya.
questions.explanation: Tante means aunt; the key uses the title Frau.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Wie geht’s? — Danke, ____.
questions.explanation: Gut means well. Rot and grau are colors.
questions.hint: Read the whole question and reply before choosing.

questions.prompt: Geht es dir gut? — ____, schlecht.
questions.explanation: The speaker feels bad, so they deny feeling good.

questions.reviewNote: The source misspells schlecht as schelcht; spelling normalized without changing the highlighted answer.

questions.prompt: Geht es dir schlecht? — ____, schlecht.
questions.explanation: The speaker confirms feeling bad.

questions.reviewNote: The source misspells schlecht as schelcht; spelling normalized without changing the highlighted answer.

groups.title: October worksheet · III. Odd one out

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? Wer – Wie – Wo – Du
questions.explanation: Wer, Wie and Wo are question words; Du is a pronoun.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? Ich – gut – Du – Er
questions.explanation: Ich, Du and Er are pronouns; gut describes a feeling.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? Morgen – super – Tag – Abend
questions.explanation: Morgen, Tag and Abend name times of day; super does not.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? Ich – Er – Sie – Wie
questions.explanation: Ich, Er and Sie are pronouns; Wie is a question word.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? super – toll – schlecht – prima
questions.explanation: The other words express a positive feeling; schlecht means bad.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? heiße – heißt – ist – heißen
questions.explanation: Heiße, heißt and heißen belong to heißen. Ist belongs to sein.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? sechs – acht – Nein – sieben
questions.explanation: The other three words are numbers; Nein means no.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? du – Ich – sie – neun
questions.explanation: The highlighted key conflicts with the natural grammatical grouping.
questions.hint: Compare pronouns with number words.
questions.reviewNote: The rendered model key highlights Ich. However du, ich and sie are pronouns and neun is a number. This disputed item is unscored; do not teach the highlighted key as a grammar rule.

questions.prompt: Was passt hier nicht? Tschüss – Grüß dich – Hallo – Hi
questions.explanation: Tschüss is a farewell; the other expressions are greetings.
questions.hint: Look for the category shared by three words.

lessons.title: Three ways to ask a name
lessons.explanation: Wer bist du? means Who are you? Wie heißt du? and Wie ist dein Name? ask a name. Keep the reply’s pattern consistent.
lessons.example: Wer bist du? → Ich bin Eva. / Wie heißt du? → Ich heiße Eva.
lessons.supportAr: السؤال عن الاسم: من أنت؟ أو ما اسمك؟ انتبه إلى شكل الجملة.

lessons.title: Ich, du and the matching verb
lessons.explanation: Use ich bin and du bist. With heißen, use ich heiße and du heißt. Mein Name takes ist.
lessons.example: Ich bin da. Du bist da. Mein Name ist Lea.
lessons.supportAr: أنا: ich bin وich heiße. أنت: du bist وdu heißt.

lessons.title: Question order
lessons.explanation: A W-question starts with the question word, then the verb. A yes/no question starts with the verb.
lessons.example: Wie heißt du? / Heißt du Lea?
lessons.supportAr: السؤال بكلمة استفهام يبدأ بها، ثم الفعل. سؤال نعم أو لا يبدأ بالفعل.

lessons.title: Ja, nein and nicht
lessons.explanation: Ja confirms. Nein is a negative answer to a question. Nicht negates something inside a sentence.
lessons.example: Bist du Tom? → Nein, ich bin nicht Tom.
lessons.supportAr: Ja تعني نعم، وNein تعني لا، وnicht تنفي جزءًا داخل الجملة.

lessons.title: Greetings during the day
lessons.explanation: Guten Morgen is for morning, Guten Tag for daytime and Guten Abend for evening. Hallo and Grüß dich are general greetings.
lessons.example: Guten Morgen! / Guten Tag! / Guten Abend!
lessons.supportAr: تحية الصباح، وتحية النهار، وتحية المساء.

lessons.title: Goodbye or good night
lessons.explanation: Tschüss and Auf Wiedersehen are goodbyes. Gute Nacht is for saying good night, especially at bedtime.
lessons.supportAr: فرّق بين الوداع وقول تصبح على خير.

lessons.title: Ask how someone is
lessons.explanation: Wie geht es dir? and Wie geht’s? ask how someone is. A reply can be positive, neutral or negative.
lessons.example: Danke, prima. / Danke, gut. / Danke, es geht. / Schlecht.
lessons.supportAr: السؤال عن الحال: كيف حالك؟ اختر ردًا يناسب الشعور.

lessons.title: Herr and Frau
lessons.explanation: Herr is a title for a man and Frau is a title for a woman. This worksheet pairs the titles with its fictional names.
lessons.supportAr: Herr لقب للرجل، وFrau لقب للمرأة. أمثلة الورقة أسماء لشخصيات تعليمية.

lessons.title: Numbers from zero to twelve
lessons.explanation: Learn the spellings as whole words. Pay special attention to fünf, sechs, sieben and zwölf.
lessons.example: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf
lessons.supportAr: تدرّب على كتابة الأعداد، وانتبه إلى النقطتين فوق الحرف في fünf وzwölf.

lessons.title: Ask and answer ages
lessons.explanation: Wie alt bist du? asks age. Answer Ich bin + number + Jahre alt. Use only the age in a pictured task; personal tasks have no fixed age.
lessons.example: Wie alt bist du? → Ich bin acht Jahre alt.
lessons.supportAr: للسؤال عن العمر: Wie alt bist du؟ وفي السؤال الشخصي اكتب عمرك أنت.

lessons.title: Yes/no questions about age
lessons.explanation: Compare the age in Bist du … Jahre alt? with the picture. Use Ja when it matches and Nein when it does not.
lessons.example: Picture age 8: Bist du sieben Jahre alt? → Nein, ich bin acht Jahre alt.
lessons.supportAr: قارن العمر في السؤال بالعمر في الصورة قبل اختيار نعم أو لا.

lessons.title: German letters and useful spellings
lessons.explanation: The PDFs sometimes print Greek β where German ß is needed. This revision uses ß. Umlauts change spelling: ä, ö, ü. Standard keyboard alternatives ae, oe, ue and ss are included for typed practice.
lessons.example: heiße / heißt / Grüß dich / Tschüss / zwölf
lessons.supportAr: استخدم ß بدل الرمز β الموجود أحيانًا في الملف. ويمكن كتابة ae وoe وue عند عدم وجود لوحة مفاتيح ألمانية.

coverageNotes: Complete source inventory: October worksheet pp1–3 plus its separate highlighted model key pp1–3, and Grade 5 booklet answer PDF pp1–27. Every numbered October item and every booklet exercise 1–22 is represented.

The October page-1 and page-2 highlights were checked visually. Its page-3 matching numbers were checked against the model key. Booklet image scenes, colored matching arrows, number pictures and birthday numerals were inspected from rendered pages.

The supplied October worksheet header says 6.KLASSE. The supplied booklet cover says 5. This bank retains the requested Grade 5 student assignment and makes no claim that the mismatched worksheet header has been corrected by the school.

October I has 22 numbered questions; its two-part items 1, 2, 5, 8 and 9 are split into both independent answer parts, yielding 27 choice items. October II has 8 ordering items, III has 9 odd-one-out items, and IV has three four-item matching sets.
October III.8 is disputed: the actual highlight selects Ich, but neun is the number among three pronouns. It is manual and unscored.
Booklet Übung 22 age is disputed: the picture shows 9 while the highlighted answer says zehn/elf. It is manual and unscored. Do not assume this is the learner’s age.
Booklet Übung 14 asks personal questions. All six responses are manual; the key’s frames are shown without assuming a name, age, wellbeing or yes/no answer.

Booklet Übung 4 contains seven individual pictured scenes, all retained. Übung 11 contains sixteen bank phrases assigned to ten observed pictures, including pictures that accept two phrases; all sixteen assignments are retained.

Booklet Übungen 18–20 retain both lines of all four pictured mini-dialogues, including the already-completed first model in Übungen 18 and 19. A multi-blank question line is practiced as one complete question, not silently dropped.
Booklet Übung 6 includes the highlighted heiße Hana response as well as the three other answer lines. Übungen 21 and 22 split each final farewell and addressee blank so every keyed part is covered.

Spelling normalization with source provenance: Greek β is replaced with German ß throughout; Wӓhle/Sӓtze are rendered as Wähle/Sätze; October I.13 Faru becomes Frau; October I.21–22 schelcht becomes schlecht; booklet Übung 22 Auf Widersehen becomes Auf Wiedersehen. These changes do not alter the supplied key selection.

Tschüss and Tschüs variants in the source are both accepted in typed farewell responses. Straight and curly apostrophes are provided as alternatives where relevant. ASCII transliterations of umlauts and ß are included for keyboard access.

Where a time-of-day illustration could be interpreted differently, the observed scene is described and the actual highlighted school phrase is used. The booklet’s neutral-face Danke, gut assignments are preserved rather than silently reinterpreted.

Cover, contents and instructional overview pages are represented by the lesson notes rather than additional scored questions. The paste-your-photo instruction above Übung 14 is a paper personalization activity and is not required for language revision.
This bank follows the supplied school key. It does not claim an independently verified exam date, cutoff or official grading scheme.
